info.title: AgentBase Runtime API
info.description:
Managed compute service for running containerized AI agents. It handles deploying, scaling, and routing requests to your agent containers, so you can focus on building the agent logic itself.

## Authentication
Every request must carry a VNG Cloud IAM OAuth2 access token in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <access_token>`. Use the **Authorize** button above to set it for "Try it out" calls. The gateway validates the token and enforces fine-grained IAM permissions on the **Agent Runtime** resource.

## Core concepts
- **Runtime**: a logical AI-agent application you own. Creating one provisions a container registry repository and an IAM Service Account for the agent.
- **Version**: an immutable snapshot of a runtime's configuration (image, env vars, startup command, flavor, autoscaling). Numbered from 1; updating a runtime always creates a new version.
- **Endpoint**: a live deployment of a specific version that actually serves traffic and exposes a public URL. The auto-created `DEFAULT` endpoint always tracks the latest version.
- **Flavor**: a named compute size (CPU/RAM/GPU) an endpoint runs on.

## API versioning
All public endpoints are versioned under the `/v1` prefix (e.g. `/v1/agent-runtimes`); prefer these paths. The older non-versioned paths (e.g. `/agent-runtimes`) remain supported for backward compatibility but are omitted from this reference.

See the full User Guide for end-to-end examples.

tags.description: Manage AI-agent runtimes, their immutable versions, and the endpoints that deploy those versions to serve traffic.

tags.name: Flavors
tags.description: Catalog of available compute sizes (CPU/RAM/GPU) that a runtime endpoint can be deployed on.

tags.name: Runtime Traces
tags.description: Query distributed traces emitted by agent runtimes (backed by Tempo). Query parameters are forwarded to the tracing backend, so its query syntax applies.

tags.name: Endpoint Inbound OAuth
tags.description: The OAuth 2.0 discovery and delegation facade of an agent endpoint, for MCP/OAuth clients connecting to that endpoint. Every route here is anonymous — clients reach them before they hold a token, so the bearer token the rest of this API requires does not apply. They are normally followed automatically from the `WWW-Authenticate: resource_metadata=` hint on a 401 from the endpoint, not called by hand.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code or refresh token
post.description: Token endpoint of the endpoint's OAuth facade. Accepts the standard `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` grant body. For an IAM-bridge endpoint the exchange is performed against VNG Cloud IAM; otherwise the request is proxied to the upstream provider and its response — including a non-2xx OAuth error envelope and `WWW-Authenticate` — is relayed verbatim, so statuses beyond those listed here can appear.

parameters.name: endpointId
parameters.description: Id of the agent endpoint this OAuth facade belongs to. Clients take it from the `resource_metadata=` hint on the endpoint's 401, rather than assembling it by hand.

200.description: The identity provider's token response, e.g. `access_token`, `token_type`, `expires_in`, `refresh_token`.

400.description: Bad request. The grant body, `Authorization` header or `Accept` header is malformed, or the grant itself was rejected (`invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_client`).

404.description: Not found. No such endpoint, or the endpoint has no inbound auth configured.

413.description: Payload too large. The token request body exceeds the limit.

500.description: Internal server error. The request could not be completed; retry it, and contact support if it persists.

502.description: Bad gateway. The endpoint's upstream identity provider could not be reached, or answered with metadata this facade cannot use.

404.description: Not found. The `state` does not resolve to an endpoint that uses the IAM bridge, so no callback is configured for it.

id.description: Unique id of the endpoint. Use it as the `{endpointId}` path variable of the endpoint operations.

agentRuntimeId.description: Id of the runtime this endpoint belongs to.

name.description: Name of the endpoint, unique within the runtime. `DEFAULT` marks the endpoint created alongside the runtime.

version.description: Deprecated: always equal to `targetVersion`. Read `targetVersion` and `liveVersion` instead, which distinguish what the endpoint is moving to from what is actually serving.

targetVersion.description: Runtime version this endpoint is meant to serve. It changes as soon as an update or version change is accepted, before that version is actually running.

liveVersion.description: Runtime version actually serving traffic right now, which lags `targetVersion` while a rollout is in flight and stays behind it if that rollout failed. `0` means nothing is serving yet — the endpoint has never completed a rollout.

currentReplicaCount.description: Replicas currently running. `0` for a stopped endpoint, or one that has not finished being created.

url.description: URL the agent is reachable at, derived from the endpoint id. A PUBLIC endpoint gets an https address on the internet; a VPC endpoint gets an http address on an internal domain and a fixed port, reachable only from that network. Assigned while the endpoint is being provisioned, so it is null until then.

outboundIps.description: Private IPs on your subnet that this endpoint uses as the source address when it calls workloads in your VPC. Allowlist these if your workloads restrict who can connect to them. They only apply to traffic into your VPC, not internet-bound traffic. To call the endpoint, use `url` instead. The list changes when the endpoint scales or its instances are replaced, and it is refreshed periodically, so it can briefly lag behind.

status.description: Stored lifecycle status of the endpoint. `ACTIVE` once it is serving and `STOPPED` once scaled down; a `WAITING_*` value means the request has been accepted but the worker has not picked it up, the matching `-ING` value means it is being carried out, and `ERROR` that it failed. Prefer `displayStatus` for anything shown to a user.

displayStatus.description: The status to show a user. Same as `status`, except that an endpoint whose update failed while an earlier version keeps serving (`liveVersion` set and behind `targetVersion`) reads as `UPDATE_FAILED` rather than a bare `ERROR`. Presentation-only: it is derived at read time and is not a stored status.

updatedAt.description: When the endpoint was last modified, including status changes made by the platform as an operation progresses.

enabled.description: Turns the GreenNode model provider on. When false no MaaS key is provisioned and the agent must call its own provider.

apiKeyName.description: Name of one of your existing MaaS API keys to call models with; the key must already exist and be active. Omit it to use the platform-managed `openclaw-service` key, which is created for you if it does not exist yet. Ignored when `enabled` is false.

botToken.description: Token of the bot the instance runs as, issued by the messaging platform.

dmPolicy.description: Who may direct-message the bot. `allowlist` restricts it to the users listed in `dmAllowedUserIds`; `pairing` instead has users pair themselves with the bot. Required whenever the channel is configured.

OpenClawChannelList.description: The messaging channels the OpenClaw instance is reachable on. Omit a channel to leave it disconnected.

telegram.description: Telegram bot the instance answers on.

zalo.description: Zalo bot the instance answers on.

greenNodeModelProvider.description: Whether the instance calls models through GreenNode MaaS. When enabled the platform provisions a MaaS API key and points the instance at it; when disabled the agent must reach its own model provider. Defaults to disabled.

environmentVariables.description: Environment variables set on the OpenClaw container.

channels.description: Messaging channels the instance talks to users on. Omit to create an instance with no channel connected.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the instance runs on, from `GET /v1/flavors?resourceType=openclaw`. Defaults to the first flavor in that list.

id.description: Unique id of the instance. Use it as the `{id}` path variable of every other OpenClaw operation.

name.description: Name of the instance, defaulted to its id when you did not supply one. It forms part of `url`.

versionId.description: Id of the published OpenClaw version the instance runs, from `GET /v1/openclaw-versions`.

url.description: URL of the instance's web console. On the create response only, the gateway token is appended as a `#token=` fragment so the link signs you straight in — treat that form of the URL as a credential. Later reads return the plain URL.

gatewayToken.description: Token for reaching the instance's gateway. Returned by the create operation only, and never retrievable afterwards, so store it when you create the instance.

greenNodeApiKeyName.description: Name of the MaaS API key the instance calls models with. Returned by the create operation only, and only when the GreenNode model provider was enabled.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the instance runs on.

status.description: Stored lifecycle status of the instance. `ACTIVE` once it is running and `STOPPED` once scaled down; an `-ING` value (`CREATING`, `UPDATING`, `DELETING`, `STOPPING`, `STARTING`, `ERROR_DELETING`) means an operation is being carried out, and `ERROR` that one failed. The internal `WAITING_*` statuses are folded into their `-ING` equivalent before being returned.

updatedAt.description: When the instance was last modified, including status changes made by the platform as an operation progresses.

poc.description: Whether the instance counts against the account's proof-of-concept quota rather than its paid quota.

LogSearchRequest.description: Which slice of the log stream to return: the time range to look in, an optional full-text filter, and where in the result set to start.

from.description: Number of matching records to skip before the returned page — an offset, not a page number.

fromTimestamp.description: Only return records at or after this instant, as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Omit for no lower bound.

toTimestamp.description: Only return records at or before this instant, as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Omit for no upper bound.

query.description: Only return records whose message contains this phrase. Omit to return every record in the range.

order.description: Sort direction on the record timestamp, newest first (`desc`) or oldest first (`asc`). Case-insensitive; defaults to `desc`.

LogRecord.description: A single line of output from the agent container.

timestamp.description: When the line was emitted, as reported by the logging backend.

content.description: The log line itself. Empty when the backend returned a record whose message could not be read.

LogSearchResult.description: One page of log records matching the search.

totalCount.description: Total number of records matching the search across the whole range, not just the ones on this page. Use it with `from` and `limit` to page through them.

AgentRuntimeEndpointCreateRequest.description: Which version of the runtime to deploy as a new endpoint, and what to call it.

name.description: Name of the endpoint. Must be unique within the runtime, which in practice rules out `DEFAULT`: that endpoint is created with the runtime and tracks its latest version.

version.description: Runtime version this endpoint serves, from `GET /v1/agent-runtimes/{id}/versions`. Unlike the DEFAULT endpoint, it stays pinned here until you change it explicitly.

AgentRuntimeAutoscaling.description: How an endpoint of this runtime scales under load. The minimum replica count is owned by the platform and is always 1, so `maxReplicas` cannot be lower than that.

maxReplicas.description: Largest number of replicas an endpoint may scale up to.

cpuUtilization.description: Average CPU utilization, as a percentage, that triggers scaling out.

memoryUtilization.description: Average memory utilization, as a percentage, that triggers scaling out.

AgentRuntimeCreateUpdateRequest.description: The configuration of a runtime version. Every update writes these values into a new immutable version and rolls the DEFAULT endpoint onto it.

description.description: Free-form description of what the agent does. Must be present, but may be an empty string.

imageUrl.description: Reference of the container image the agent runs from, in Docker `[registry/]repository[:tag|@digest]` form. The registry must be reachable from the public internet: an image whose registry host resolves to a private or internal address is rejected.

imageAuth.description: Credentials used to pull the image. Must be present; send it with `enabled: false` for an image that needs no authentication.

environmentVariables.description: Environment variables set on the agent container. Names the platform injects itself (the `GREENNODE_*` and `OTEL_*` variables) are reserved and rejected, since an injected value would otherwise silently replace yours.

networkConfig.description: Where the endpoints of this runtime are reachable from. Omit for a public endpoint.

inboundAuth.description: How requests reaching the endpoints are authenticated. Omit to leave the endpoints unauthenticated (mode NONE). Only supported in PUBLIC network mode.

protocol.description: Wire protocol the agent speaks. MCP makes the endpoint answer authentication failures with the MCP error envelope and the OAuth discovery hint instead of a plain HTTP status. Defaults to HTTP.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the endpoints run on, from `GET /v1/flavors`. The flavor must be enabled and must support the resource type of the chosen network mode (`agent-runtime` for PUBLIC, `agent-runtime-vpc` for VPC).

autoscaling.description: How the endpoints scale under load. Required.

AgentRuntimeImageAuth.description: Registry credentials used to pull the agent image. Always required on a create or update; send it with `enabled: false` for an image that needs no authentication.

enabled.description: Whether the image needs credentials to pull. When false the rest of this object is ignored.

useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials.description: Pull the image with the platform's own AgentBase registry credentials instead of `username`/`password`. Only accepted when the image lives in the AgentBase registry.

username.description: Registry username. Required when `enabled` is true and `useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials` is false.

password.description: Registry password or access token. Required when `enabled` is true and `useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials` is false. Stored encrypted and never returned by the API.

AgentRuntimeInboundAuth.description: How the platform authenticates requests arriving at the runtime's endpoints, before they reach the agent container. Omit the whole object to leave the endpoints unauthenticated. Only supported in PUBLIC network mode.

mode.description: NONE lets every request through. IAM requires a VNG Cloud IAM token belonging to the account that owns the endpoint. JWT verifies a bearer token issued by your own identity provider, configured under `jwt`.

jwt.description: Identity provider settings used to verify inbound bearer tokens. Required when `mode` is JWT, and ignored otherwise.

AgentRuntimeInboundAuthJwt.description: Verification settings for JWT inbound auth: where the signing keys come from, and which claims a token must carry to be accepted. Required when the inbound-auth mode is JWT, and ignored otherwise.

source.description: Where the signing keys come from. DISCOVERY fetches them from the provider's metadata document at `discoveryUrl`. JWKS uses the key set pasted into `jwks`, for a provider the platform cannot reach. The field the other source does not use is dropped.

jwks.description: Public JSON Web Key Set used to verify token signatures, as an RFC 7517 `{"keys": [...]}` document. Required when `source` is JWKS. Must be at most 32 KiB and 10 keys, and must contain public keys only — a key carrying private material is rejected.

discoveryUrl.description: URL of the provider's metadata document. Required when `source` is DISCOVERY. Must be https, must not resolve to a private or internal address, and must end with `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` so the issuer can be derived from it.

principalClaim.description: Claim whose value identifies the caller and is forwarded to the agent. Defaults to `sub`.

AgentRuntimeNetworkConfig.description: Where the runtime's endpoints are reachable from. Omit the whole object to expose them publicly.

mode.description: PUBLIC exposes the endpoints on the internet. VPC places them inside one of your VPCs, reachable only from that network; VPC mode does not support `allowedCidrs` or inbound auth.

vpcId.description: Id of the VPC the endpoints are placed in. Required in VPC mode; the VPC must have DNS enabled.

subnetId.description: Id of the subnet within `vpcId` the endpoints are placed in. Required in VPC mode.

AgentRuntimeDto.description: An agent runtime: the logical agent application, without the per-version configuration. Use the version and endpoint operations to see what it currently runs and where.

id.description: Unique id of the runtime. Use it as the `{id}` path variable of every other runtime operation.

description.description: Not populated: the runtime itself stores no description, so this is always null. The description supplied on create or update belongs to the version — read it from the list-versions operation instead.

status.description: Stored lifecycle status of the runtime. `ACTIVE` once it is serving and `STOPPED` once scaled down; an `-ING` value (`CREATING`, `UPDATING`, `DELETING`, `STOPPING`, `STARTING`, `ROLLING_BACK_UPDATE`) means an operation is still in flight, and `ERROR` that the last one failed. `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ERROR` is reported by the get operation when the runtime's IAM Service Account no longer checks out. Prefer `displayStatus` for anything shown to a user.

displayStatus.description: The status to show a user. Same as `status`, except that a runtime whose DEFAULT endpoint failed an update while an earlier version keeps serving reads as `UPDATE_FAILED` rather than a bare `ERROR`. Presentation-only: it is derived at read time and is not a stored status.

statusReason.description: Why the runtime is in its current status, when there is something to say. Only populated by the get operation, and only for `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ERROR`; null otherwise.

updatedAt.description: When the runtime was last modified, including status changes made by the platform as an operation progresses.

poc.description: Whether the runtime counts against the account's proof-of-concept quota rather than its paid quota.

environmentVariables.description: Environment variables set on the agent container. Names the platform injects itself (the `GREENNODE_*` and `OTEL_*` variables) are reserved and rejected, since an injected value would otherwise silently replace yours.

inboundAuth.description: How requests reaching the endpoints are authenticated. Omit to leave the endpoints unauthenticated (mode NONE). Only supported in PUBLIC network mode.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the endpoints run on, from `GET /v1/flavors`. The flavor must be enabled and must support the resource type of the chosen network mode (`agent-runtime` for PUBLIC, `agent-runtime-vpc` for VPC).

name.description: Name of the runtime. Cannot be changed after creation.

poc.description: Whether to create the runtime against the account's proof-of-concept quota instead of its paid quota. Only accounts enabled for PoC may set this.

error.description: Machine-readable OAuth error code, such as `invalid_request`, `invalid_grant` or `not_found`. This is the field to branch on.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the failure. Meant to be read, not matched on.

useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials.description: Whether the pull uses the platform's own AgentBase registry credentials rather than a username and password you supplied.

username.description: Registry username, when you supplied one. Null when the platform's AgentBase registry credentials are used, since that pair is not yours to see.

mode.description: `NONE` lets every request through, `IAM` requires a VNG Cloud IAM token belonging to the account that owns the endpoint, and `JWT` verifies a bearer token against the `jwt` settings below.

jwt.description: Token verification settings. Present only when `mode` is `JWT`; null otherwise.

AgentRuntimeInboundAuthJwtDto.description: JWT verification settings of a version. Every field is echoed back: none of them is a secret, since the key material here is public by construction.

source.description: Where the signing keys come from, `DISCOVERY` or `JWKS`. Only the field that source uses is populated; the other is null.

jwks.description: The configured public JSON Web Key Set, when `source` is `JWKS`. Safe to expose: validation rejects any key carrying private material.

principalClaim.description: Claim whose value identifies the caller. Always populated, defaulting to `sub`.

networkConfig.description: Network placement of the endpoints running this version.

inboundAuth.description: Inbound authentication settings of the endpoints running this version.

protocol.description: Wire protocol the agent speaks, `HTTP` or `MCP`. Versions written before this field existed read as `HTTP`.

AgentRuntimeEndpointMetrics.description: Resource usage of an endpoint over the requested time range, as one time series per metric. value.description: Value measured at that instant. Its unit is stated by the field carrying this series.

MetricDataPointLong.description: One sample of a time series: when it was taken, and what was measured.

value.description: Value measured at that instant. Its unit is stated by the field carrying this series.

KubeEventDto.description: A Kubernetes event recorded for an endpoint, useful for diagnosing why it is not becoming ready. Only recent events are retained.

message.example: Failed to pull image "registry.example.com/my-agent:1.0": not found

lastTimestamp.description: When this event was last seen. A repeating event keeps one entry and moves this timestamp forward.

ListResponseAgentRuntimeEndpointDto.description: One page of a listing, with the counters needed to walk the rest of it.

page.description: Page this response covers, echoing the requested `page`. 1-based.

pageSize.description: Items per page, echoing the requested `size`. The last page may hold fewer items than this.

totalPage.description: Total number of pages at this page size. Requesting a higher `page` returns an empty `listData`.

totalItem.description: Total number of items across every page.

ProtectedResourceMetadata.description: RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata: what a client needs in order to get a token for this endpoint. Fields RFC 9728 marks optional are omitted rather than sent empty.

resource.description: Canonical identifier of the endpoint as a protected resource. Always present.

bearerAuth.description: VNG Cloud IAM OAuth2 access token. Obtain a token by exchanging your Service Account clientId/clientSecret at the IAM token endpoint (grant_type=client_credentials), then send it as `Bearer <access_token>`.
